title: Homeward Porkchop
tagline: The return leg Aster does not plan yet: a body-to-Earth porkchop that colours Earth-arrival v-infinity and refuses, in so many words, to price delivered mass.
pitch: Pick one of six bodies (the five NHATS validation targets 99942, 101955, 2000 SG344, 2001 GP2, 1999 AO10, plus 433 Eros) and the page draws a porkchop whose axes are body-departure date and flight time, over the 2026-2040 Earth span. Each cell holds a Lambert solution from the body's Kepler-propagated state to Earth's Horizons state: departure v-infinity at the body (the push a return vehicle must buy), Earth-arrival v-infinity, its declination in the same asin(vz/|v|) convention Aster uses for DLA, and the implied 125 km entry speed. Click a cell and the side panel shows the return stack lines it can defend and, where the outbound page shows a delivered-mass card, a structured refusal card: code out_of_envelope, reason 'launch-vehicle payload curves describe Earth departure from a parking orbit; none applies to a body-departure leg', what_would_help 'a return-vehicle mass model, or an Earth-capture envelope (K2)'. Every minimum states the lattice it came from, as DEC-19-2 demands. The arrival v-infinity column is the exact quantity the kernel doc names as the Aster-to-Skyhook interface, so this is the K1 half of that link, built without touching K2.
whyNow: K1 return-leg porkchop, /home/user/asteroid-mining-planner/strategy/IDEA_KERNELS_2026-09.md §1 row 3, §3 item 2 and §6.1 ('the remaining work is the Earth-as-departure assumptions, not the arrival quantity'); the shipped stack's symmetric-return assumption at src/v2/porkchop/delta-v.ts:36 (departureDvFromVInf = vInfArr) is what a real return leg replaces; SLICE_19_5_FOUNDING.md §1 parks K1 for Slice 20+.
computes: Inputs: body elements (aKm, e, i, Om, w, M, epochTdbJd; FRAME_HELIO_J2000_ECLIPTIC) and anchor state from the catalog excerpt; weekly-thinned Earth records (jdTdb, r, v in km, km/s, ICRF) with cubic Hermite in between; GM_SUN 1.32712440018e20 and obliquity 84381.448 arcsec cited to src/v2/core. Math: Kepler propagation of the body, rotated ecliptic to ICRF; Lambert (own clean-room universal-variable implementation, M=0, both directions) from r_body(t_dep) to r_earth(t_dep+tof); v_inf_dep = |v1 - v_body|, v_inf_arr = |v2 - v_earth|, arrival declination asin(vz/|v_inf_arr|), entry speed sqrt(v_inf_arr^2 + 2*398600.4418/(6378.137+125)). Grid: ~150 departure dates x 60 flight times (30-720 d). Outputs: colormap of v_inf_arr (and a toggle for v_inf_dep), pinned-cell readout with the lattice label, a refusal object for delivered mass on every cell, and a 'frame check' line showing |propagated(epoch) - anchor| in km.
dataNeeded: tools/snapshot.mjs picks asteroids.asteroid-99942, asteroid-101955, 'asteroid-2000 SG344', 'asteroid-2001 GP2', 'asteroid-1999 AO10', asteroid-433 from tests/fixtures/v2/nea-catalog-slice9.json (~0.9 KB each, ~6 KB); a derived weekly thinning (every 7th record, 783 of 5,479) of targets.earth.records from src/v2/data/horizons-inner-solar-system-2026-2040.json recorded with --sidecar-only (~115 KB) plus the first 91 daily Earth records of tests/fixtures/v2/horizons-inner-system-90d.json for the held-out interpolation test (~15 KB); the five NHATS files tests/fixtures/v2/nhats-validation-targets/*.json picked to des, fullname, computed, min_dv_traj (~4 KB); the M=0 cells of tests/fixtures/v2/lambert-multi-rev-pinned-cells.json (9.5 KB) as the solver oracle. Total ~150 KB.
existingOverlap: Aster plans outbound only: src/v2/porkchop/grid-compute.ts fixes Earth as departure and the body as arrival; vInfArr is computed per branch and persisted in lambert-screen-cache.json bestWindows, but no return leg exists anywhere (grep of src/, mcp/, tests/ for return-leg, body-to-Earth: nothing). MCP tools porkchop_scan and explain_cell are outbound. This candidate swaps endpoints and adds the arrival-declination and entry-speed readouts and the mandatory refusal; it does not reuse izzo.ts (TypeScript, protected) and says so.
honestyRisks: (1) A home-made Lambert solver could be silently wrong: it is tested against the pinned oracle cells to 1e-8 relative and the README labels it idea-bank fidelity, with izzo.ts as the solver that would ship. (2) Frame error: catalog elements are ecliptic, Horizons vectors ICRF; the test propagates each body to its element epoch and asserts |r - anchor.positionKm| < 1 km, so the obliquity rotation is established by measurement (INV-021), not by label. (3) Weekly Earth sampling: the analytic Hermite bound (h^4/384)*w^4*r is ~82 km at 7 d for a circular 1 au orbit [Likely]; the test measures it against held-out daily records and the page prints the measured bound; Slice 18 found 1,000 km along-track moves C3 by ~0.001%, so this is disclosed as below the lattice noise. (4) Body-departure dV = v_inf ignores body gravity (Eros escape ~10 m/s); disclosed per cell. (5) Delivered mass: no number is ever rendered; the card is a refusal object and the DOM test asserts no kg string appears. (6) Two-body only; L1/L2 tier badge from docs/tier-sizing-per-body.json shown on the body picker, L0 bodies refused with the tier sentence. (7) NHATS trajectories are min-total-dV round trips at 400 km/125 km conventions, used as an external anchor with residuals printed, not as truth.
testPlan: node --test: (a) solver reproduces every M=0 pinned cell's v1/v2 to <= 1e-8 relative and the recorded c3/vInfDep/vInfArr; (b) Kepler+rotation at epoch matches anchor.positionKm within 1 km for all six bodies; (c) Hermite on the weekly Earth excerpt vs the 91 held-out daily records: max position error < 200 km and <= 2x the analytic bound, the measured number written to example.txt; (d) NHATS reconciliation: for each of the five targets, solve the return leg at NEO departure = launch + dur_out + dur_at and TOF = dur_ret from min_dv_traj; assert |v_inf_dep - vrel_dep_neo| < 0.5 km/s and |entry speed - v_arr_earth| < 0.5 km/s, and print all residuals; (e) every cell's delivered-mass field is a refusal object with code out_of_envelope and a non-empty what_would_help; (f) the lattice label is derived from the grid parameters, not a literal (string equality against a computed label); tools/smoke.mjs at 390 px with a tap on a cell.
landing: asteroid-mining-planner: a return-grid-compute.ts beside src/v2/porkchop/grid-compute.ts (endpoints swapped, izzo.ts as solver), a ?leg=return mode on /v2/porkchop/ in src/v2/app/porkchop/main.ts, and a refusal path in the cost card. To ship it must: use izzo.ts and the committed daily Earth ephemeris instead of this bank's solver and thinning, pass the multi-agent math audit (src/v2/core is protected; dispatch required), get a K1 charter and founding-doc DECs for the body-departure assumptions, and surface the arrival v-infinity in the MCP envelope for K2.
notes: K1 is named 'highest thesis value per unit cost' in IDEA_KERNELS §3; verified no return-leg code exists in src/mcp/tests. Large build with a clean-room Lambert solver, but the oracle cells and refusal design are sound.
K1 is the top named kernel; verified delta-v.ts:32-34 departureDvFromVInf=vInfArr, IDEA_KERNELS §6.1 exists, no return-leg code in src/mcp/tests; own Lambert is heavy but pinned oracle cells exist.

K1 is the kernel doc's own top-value shortlist item (IDEA_KERNELS §3 item 2), but a clean-room universal-variable Lambert plus Kepler plus Hermite plus a 9,000-cell grid for six bodies is a multi-day build; checked lambert-multi-rev-pinned-cells.json and it holds ONE M=0 cell (apophis-M0), not a set, so the 'every M=0 pinned cell' oracle is thin and only the NHATS residuals anchor the solver.
